newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen flat or down next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen flat or down next week.

text.p: Polish shares are seen flat or down next week as positive and negative factors clash amid a market that seemed fairly valued, analysts said.

They said a fall was likely on Monday, starting off the week shortened by holidays on Thursday and Friday, and that the main WIG index, which rose 1.8 percent this week to 16,669.1 points, could drift between 16,000 and 17,000 points.

"It's hard to say if there'll be one more fall or a few but we seem to be entering a phase where there are no big moves of the index in either direction," said Artur Kobos, a trader at ING Baring Securities in Warsaw.
Analysts said recent optimistic inflation and GDP forecasts were a good sign but that this year's several large primary offers could draw cash from listed shares in the short term.
Last Friday the chief analyst at the government's Centre for Strategic Studies (CSS) said inflation may dip to about 15 percent this month from 16.6 percent in March.

On Thursday the independent Gdansk Market Economy Institute (IBnGR) said gross domestic product (GDP) grew 7.6 percent in the first quarter of 1997 against five percent in the same quarter of last year.
But analysts said the state treasury sale of 2,976,560 shares in metals trader and producer Impexmetal at a minimum price of 36 zlotys, which ends on Wednesday, could draw capital from the bourse.
They said large public offerings due at mid-year, such as those of Bank Handlowy SA and copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA, could help send the market down more significantly.

Many analysts said the market seemed fairly valued at current levels though some said stocks were still a bit expensive after the surge earlier this year and that the bourse might soon fall below 16,000 points.
They said company earnings were mixed so far this year despite some good March data by several firms and that some firms might not fulfil this year's earnings forecasts.

"Some forecasts are not coming true," said Piotr Leszczuk of Bank Slaski brokerage, giving as an example trader Universal, which made a pre-tax profit of 6.3 million zlotys in the first quarter after predicting one of 35 million for 1997.

Leszczuk said paper firm Celuloza Swiecie's could fall from Friday's bourse debut at 21.5 zlotys because of weak first quarter earnings, though more bullish observers saw Poland's largest paper firm staying between 20 and 22 zlotys.
This week's top gainer Remak rose 30 percent amid the current good construction climate and the news it saw its net profit rising this year to 987,000 from 100,000 zlotys.
Analysts also said the Warsaw bourse remained vulnerable to sharp price moves on foreign bourses, reflected by Wednesday's 1.8-percent rise after a Dow Jones surge.
